Capital is a Social Relation, Not Just Matter
A cotton-spinning machine is
a machine for spinning cotton.
It is no more capital than gold is
money, or a Negro is a slave.
It only becomes Capital within a
definite social relation: the dominion
of past, accumulated, materialized
labour over immediate, living labour.
Capital does not exist because accumulated labor serves living labor. It exists
because living labor serves accumulated labor to multiply its exchange value.

What the Worker Yields
A portion of existing means of subsistence.

Living productive activity. The creative force that
not only replaces what was consumed, but vields
a greater value than it previously possessed.
The worker consumes the capitalist's money unproductively (it is gone). The
capitalist consumes the worker's labor reproductively (it becomes more capital).
